chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Lays al-Muradi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The most knowledgeable of the people with Allah is the one most satisfied with the Judgement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What is the sign of true knowledge of God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this hadith from al-Kafi links gnosis (ma'rifah) directly to the state of the heart, suggesting that intellectual knowledge is incomplete without the spiritual tranquility of rida (contentment). Scholars emphasize that 'satisfaction with divine decree' is not passive resignation but an active recognition of Allah's wisdom, serving as the ultimate proof of a believer's true understanding of the Divine. This concept is central to the development of the 'perfect believer' (al-insan al-kamil) who aligns their will with God's will.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Lays Al Murady, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The most knowledgeable of the people with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the one most satisfied of them with the Judgement of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from Layth al- Muradi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
The most knowledgeable among people is the one who agrees with the decisions of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy.’”
